findings.antecedent: Cast shadows
findings.consequent: Recovery of spatial arrangement (spatial layout)
findings.quote: Among all these roles, we found that cast shadows were perceptually most relevant for the recovery of spatial arrangement, especially when the shadow is in motion.

findings.antecedent: Cast shadows
findings.consequent: Recovery of surface shape (casting object or background)
findings.quote: As we will show, the human visual system does not effectively use cast shadows as cues to surface shape, despite the potential reliability of the information they provide.

findings.antecedent: Moving cast shadows
findings.consequent: Perception of an object moving in depth
findings.quote: Particularly striking is the observation that moving cast shadows can produce a very vivid impression of an object moving in depth.

findings.antecedent: Manipulation of an object's cast shadow motion
findings.consequent: Perceived trajectory of the object
findings.quote: Moreover, simply manipulating the motion of an object's cast shadow can dramatically change the perceived trajectory of the object.

findings.antecedent: Cast shadow on a folded card (static image)
findings.consequent: Disambiguation of card's shape (convex/concave)
findings.quote: Even though the shape of the shadow in Fig. 2 is theoretically sufficient to disambiguate the shape of the card, the shape remains ambiguous perceptually.

findings.antecedent: Static cast shadow detaching from an object (Fig. 3)
findings.consequent: Perception of the object moving in depth
findings.quote: By moving only the cast shadow of a static object in a scene, we were able to induce a strong percept of object motion in depth (despite the fact that the object did not move or change size in the image).

findings.antecedent: Penumbra surrounding shadow boundary
findings.consequent: Perceived depth motion of object (from shadow translation)
findings.quote: The proportion of times the square is perceived moving in depth increases when a penumbra is surrounding the shadow boundary...

findings.antecedent: Shadow displacement consistent with light above scene
findings.consequent: Perceived depth motion of object (from shadow translation)
findings.quote: ...when the shadow displacement is consistent with a light located above the scene...

findings.antecedent: Darker cast shadow (rather than light)
findings.consequent: Perceived depth motion of object (from shadow translation)
findings.quote: ...and when the shadow is dark rather than light.

findings.antecedent: Changing contrast, opacity, or shape of cast shadow (in ball-in-box animation)
findings.consequent: Perceived trajectory of the ball in space
findings.quote: Interestingly, the perceived trajectory of the ball in space was not affected by changing the contrast, the opacity or even the shape of the shadow.

findings.antecedent: Image sequence generated by moving the light source (instead of object)
findings.consequent: Perception of object moving in depth
findings.quote: Observers perceived a square moving in depth in Fig. 3 even when the image sequence was obtained by moving the light source rather than the square.

findings.antecedent: Adding more evidence that light was moving (e.g., more objects)
findings.consequent: Perceived trajectory of the ball
findings.quote: Adding more evidence that the light was actually moving, such as adding more objects in the scene, did not affect the perceived trajectory of the ball.

findings.antecedent: Changing shading to suggest alternative illumination directions
findings.consequent: Perceived trajectory of the ball
findings.quote: Changing the shading on the ball to suggest illumination from alternative directions only changed the perceived trajectory of the ball slightly – not nearly as much as was predicted by the new light source location.

findings.antecedent: Shadow motion (e.g., square moving in depth)
findings.consequent: Perception of self-motion
findings.quote: This ambiguity between observer and object motion was never experienced: none of the observers in our experiments ever reported a perception of self-motion.

findings.antecedent: Cast shadow cue for dynamic spatial layout
findings.consequent: Overriding of generic viewpoint constraint, constant size cue, and rigidity constraint
findings.quote: The fact that the cast shadow cue can override the generic viewpoint constraint, the constant size cue as well as the rigidity constraint is a qualitative index of the strength of the cast shadow cue for dynamic spatial layout perception.

findings.antecedent: Correlated motion between an object and its cast shadow (dynamic scenes)
findings.consequent: Reliable shadow labeling and linking of objects with shadows
findings.quote: In dynamic scenes, a feature appears which can very reliably determine proper shadow labeling: the relative motion of an object and its cast shadow is constrained to follow a line connecting the object to the light source.

findings.antecedent: Object-shadow correlated motion (dynamic scenes)
findings.consequent: Robustness of phenomenal percept of motion to violations of shadow luminance constraints
findings.quote: In the ball-in-a-box movie, the object itself is moving, hence the object-shadow correlated motion which appears in the animation would be accidental if caused by anything other than an object casting a shadow. It therefore provides a strong cue to shadow labeling, and the phenomenal percept of motion is more robust to violations of shadow luminance constraints.

findings.antecedent: Object-shadow correlated motion (static object, trivial correlation)
findings.consequent: Efficacy of shadow cue when luminance constraints are violated
findings.quote: In this special case, object-shadow correlated motion does not provide a reliable cue to shadow labeling, and violations of shadow luminance constraints (such as making the shadow lighter than the background) do reduce the efficacy of the shadow cue.

findings.antecedent: Cast shadows
findings.consequent: Global rather than local information about spatial layout
findings.quote: Cast shadows are non-commensurate with other depth cues because they provide global rather than local information about spatial layout.

findings.antecedent: Cast shadows
findings.consequent: Interaction with other depth cues (size change, binocular disparity, motion parallax)
findings.quote: Nevertheless, an interaction between cast shadows and other depth cues has been found experimentally, in particular the cues of size change, binocular disparity and motion parallax.
